messages:
customer-acme: Hey team — since ~23:40 UTC our calls to /v1/generate are returning 502/504 and timeouts. A handful of requests succeed but most fail. Request id: req_8a3f. Can someone look?

james.support: Sorry you're hitting this, we're on it. Can you paste a raw curl + response headers if available? Also which region (us-west/us-east)?

customer-acme: Here's a minimal repro: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -d '{"model":"rwd-1","prompt":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 23:41:02 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: req_8a3f
Content-Length: 125

{"error":{"message":"upstream read timeout","type":"gateway_error"}}
```

nora-cs: Customer in us-west-2, steady traffic but error spike started ~23:36 UTC. Notified support tier-1 and asked for escalation.

lina-oncall: Looking at infra graphs — memcached/prefix-cache GET latency jumped from ~2ms to 250-600ms at 23:35 in us-west-2. Error rate on runtime proxy also spikes with 502/504. KV error counters show timeouts and TCP retries.

tom-runtime: Confirmed in logs: runtime saw many cache GETs returning ERR/ETIMEDOUT and then fallback path raising upstream timeout. Example log: 
```
2026-03-17T23:36:12Z error=kvcache.get timeout key=prefix:acct:12345 attempt=3 err=ETIMEDOUT
2026-03-17T23:36:12Z warn=request failed upstream_timeout request_id=req_8a3f route=/v1/generate
```

lina-oncall: Are we seeing memcached node OOMs or network flaps? Metrics: memcached evictions ↑, active connections spiking, retransmits up ~400%.

tom-runtime: Quick check of the memcached cluster in us-west-2: 2 nodes reported heavy GC/oom_kill messages on host-level, network interface errors on eth0 on node-a. Could be host-level networking degradation.

james.support: Customer asked for ETA. Can we surface a mitigation (fail open / increase timeout) while infra team investigates?

lina-oncall: Doing two things now: (1) route new requests to read-through fallback (disable prefix cache) for affected pools, (2) increase memcached client read timeout from 500ms -> 1500ms to reduce immediate 5xxs. Applying changes to us-west runtime pool.

deploy-bot: memcached-client-config update deploy started for pool=us-west-2-runtime by lina-oncall (change: read_timeout_ms=1500)

lina-oncall: Also kicked a rolling restart of memcached nodes, but keeping one node up per AZ. Restart in-progress on node-a.

tom-runtime: After config change we're seeing error rate drop ~80% within 45s. Some residual spikes while nodes restart. Backend traces show successful fallback to DB/cache-miss path.

nora-cs: Customer reports fewer 502s. They still see occasional ~1/200 requests fail but traffic mostly normal.

customer-acme: Thanks — much better now. Our service is back to normal, will keep monitoring on our side.

james.support: Marking as mitigated for now. Next steps: runbook updates, root-cause analysis (possible host network flaps causing memcached instability), and follow up with customer with timeline.

lina-oncall: Agreed. I'll open an incident ticket and add hosts to infra postmortem. Action items: 
- infra: investigate NIC errors and host-level OOMs on memcached nodes (tom-runtime + infra)
- runtime: add circuit-breaker on prefix cache path to fail open earlier and reduce upstream timeouts (lina-oncall + tom-runtime)
- devel: add alert for memcached retransmit > 200% and sustained GET latency > 100ms (prom team)

tom-runtime: Quick patch idea: change prefix cache client to treat ETIMEDOUT as soft-failure and fallback immediately (no retry) for 1 minute after spike; will draft PR.

james.support: I'll send a customer note with the mitigation summary and an ETA for full RCA.

deploy-bot: memcached-node-restart finished for node-a (node-a -> healthy). Node-b health checks passing.

lina-oncall: Final check: 5xx rate back to baseline for us-west-2, memcached GET p50~3ms, p95~12ms. Closing escalation — will update incident ticket with timeline.

customer-acme: Confirmed — all green on our end. Thanks for fast response! :tada:
